part.text: The annual records show 110 motorists killed in 2013 and 81 in 2025, while motorist-fatal crashes as a share of all reported crashes rose from about 0.050% to 0.088%. I’m charting both as distinct crash-data perspectives; neither is a per-mile risk measure.

input.command: python3 -c 'import duckdb, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt; from pathlib import Path; out=Path("out"); df=duckdb.sql("SELECT year(crash_date) AS year, count(*) AS crashes, sum(number_of_motorist_killed) AS motorist_deaths, count(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_motorist_killed > 0) AS motorist_fatal_crashes FROM read_parquet(\"data/crashes.parquet\") WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1").df(); df["motorist_fatal_crashes_per_1000_reported_crashes"] = df["motorist_fatal_crashes"] / df["crashes"] * 1000; df.to_csv(out / "values_1.csv", index=False); df[["year", "crashes", "motorist_deaths", "motorist_fatal_crashes", "motorist_fatal_crashes_per_1000_reported_crashes"]].to_csv(out / "values_2.csv", index=False); plt.figure(figsize=(9, 5.2)); plt.plot(df["year"], df["motorist_deaths"], marker="o", linewidth=2.3, color="#1769aa"); plt.xticks(df["year"], rotation=45); plt.ylabel("Motorists killed (persons)"); plt.xlabel("Crash year"); plt.title("Motorists killed in NYC crashes, 2013–2025"); plt.suptitle("Annual count; does not account for miles driven", y=0.94, fontsize=10, color="#555555"); plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25); plt.annotate("110", (2013, 110), xytext=(6, 8), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=9); plt.annotate("81", (2025, 81), xytext=(-18, 8), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=9); plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.92)); plt.savefig(out / "option_1.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close(); plt.figure(figsize=(9, 5.2)); plt.plot(df["year"], df["motorist_fatal_crashes_per_1000_reported_crashes"], marker="o", linewidth=2.3, color="#b34b36"); plt.xticks(df["year"], rotation=45); plt.ylabel("Motorist-fatal crashes per 1,000 reported crashes"); plt.xlabel("Crash year"); plt.title("Share of reported crashes with a motorist death, 2013–2025"); plt.suptitle("Crash-based severity proxy; not a per-mile risk measure", y=0.94, fontsize=10, color="#555555"); plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25); start=df.loc[df.year.eq(2013), "motorist_fatal_crashes_per_1000_reported_crashes"].iloc[0]; end=df.loc[df.year.eq(2025), "motorist_fatal_crashes_per_1000_reported_crashes"].iloc[0]; plt.annotate(f"{start:.3f}", (2013, start), xytext=(6, 8), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=9); plt.annotate(f"{end:.3f}", (2025, end), xytext=(-30, 8), textcoords="offset points", fontsize=9); plt.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.92)); plt.savefig(out / "option_2.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight"); plt.close(); print(df.to_string(index=False))'

Recorded motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, but that count cannot establish whether deaths per mile driven declined (chart: `out/option_1.png`; values: `out/values_1.csv`).
